name: FathomDB
tagline: Early YC-backed MySQL-as-a-service on AWS and Rackspace; the team joined Meteor in 2014 and it closed.
description: FathomDB was a Y Combinator startup, founded in 2008, that sold hosted MySQL as a service on Amazon and Rackspace clouds and claims to have launched the first relational database-as-a-service, around the time Amazon RDS appeared. Customers got a hosted MySQL server instead of running database VMs themselves, and the team also contributed early code to OpenStack's database-as-a-service effort. FathomDB later started building a 'cloud-first' relational database but did not finish it; in 2014 the company joined Meteor, the JavaScript application platform, and the hosted service was wound down. Its significance is historical, as one of the first database-as-a-service businesses.
statusNote: The FathomDB team joined Meteor in 2014 and the hosted MySQL service was shut down. Use Amazon RDS, PlanetScale or another managed MySQL.

pricing.notes: Was sold as a hosted service; detailed pricing has not survived and the service no longer exists.

strengths: One of the first hosted relational database services, on both AWS and Rackspace
Stock MySQL compatibility, so applications needed no changes
weaknesses: Customers had to migrate elsewhere when the team joined Meteor
useCases: Historical reference for the early database-as-a-service market
Background on how hosted MySQL evolved before RDS and PlanetScale dominated
notIdealFor: Any current workload: the service no longer exists
